explain.say: Concrete cracks when stretched, so engineers use a clever trick: squeeze it before it is ever loaded. In pre-tensioned concrete, high-strength steel strands are first stretched very tight between strong anchors.

explain.say: Then the strands are cut free from the anchors. They try to spring back to their shorter length, but the concrete holds them, so they squeeze the whole beam, especially along the bottom.

explain.say: When the beam is loaded, bending tries to stretch the bottom, but first it has to undo that built-in squeeze. So the concrete stays in compression and does not crack, letting beams be slimmer and span farther.

faq.a: It is concrete squeezed by tightly stretched steel before it carries any load. Loads then only reduce the squeeze, so the concrete never has to resist much stretching and stays crack-free.
Tendons are high-strength steel wires, strands or bars that are stretched very hard. They are several times stronger than ordinary reinforcing bars.

faq.q: How does stretching steel make concrete stronger?
faq.a: Stretched steel wants to shorten. Once it is locked into the concrete, it pulls the ends together and squeezes the beam, which cancels out the stretching a load would cause.
asks: Why do tendons squeeze the beam?

faq.q: What is the difference between pre-tensioning and post-tensioning?
faq.a: In pre-tensioning, the steel is stretched before the concrete is poured, usually in a factory. In post-tensioning, the steel runs through ducts in hardened concrete and is stretched and anchored afterwards, often on site.
In bridge beams, long-span floors, railway sleepers, car parks and water tanks: wherever slim, crack-free concrete must carry heavy loads over long distances.

facts: French engineer Eugène Freyssinet developed practical prestressed concrete, patenting his method in 1928.
Most modern concrete railway sleepers are pre-tensioned.

quiz.say: Why is the steel in prestressed concrete stretched before the beam is used?
quiz.show: The steel is stretched first so that…

options.show: The concrete is squeezed and resists cracking
options.say: The concrete is squeezed and resists cracking

quiz.why: The stretched steel squeezes the concrete, so loads only reduce that squeeze instead of stretching the concrete.

wrong.1: Prestressing lets beams be slimmer, but stretching the steel does not itself change the weight.
wrong.2: Rust protection comes from the concrete cover, not from stretching.
